title: LauzHack 2026 - Policies
text:
LauzHack 2026 - Policies

# Acceptance

Because the main LauzHack event typically receives far more applications than we have physical space to host, we cannot accept everyone. Our acceptance process is a random draw done in batches that balances EPFL and non-EPFL participation.

The earlier you finish the application process, the more chances you have to be accepted. Acceptance decisions do not take into account your CV nor personal details such as dietary restrictions.

If you apply as a group, we guarantee that if one member of the group is accepted, then all others are also accepted. You can form a team with whoever you want during the event, regardless of who you applied with. Accepted participants may not be replaced by someone else nor add someone to their group after acceptance.

Application decisions are final. If you are rejected, the decision is about space constraints, not about you personally. Please do not contact us asking if you could participate anyway.

# Sleeping and Accommodation

You are welcome to sleep during the event, including going home to sleep if you live nearby. Depending on where you come from, you may need accommodation before or after the event. You can include the cost of hostels/hotels/AirBnB in the travel reimbursement up to the relevant limit, as described in the travel reimbursement section below.

# America250: Student Innovators Invited to Compete in National Startup Challenge

Undergraduate students are invited to apply for America’s Startup, a national pitch competition highlighting early-stage business ideas. Submit your proposal by March 31, 2026.

- published: 2026/03/05
- contact: Office of Strategic Marketing and Communications
- email: unonews@unomaha.edu

America’s Startup is a national collegiate startup competition designed to spotlight and support student innovators at the earliest stages of building a business. Participants submit a proposal and pitch video outlining their idea. Selected teams advance through a multi-stage review process that includes a live pitch experience.

📅 Entries are due by 11:59 P.M. Eastern Time on March 31, 2026.

America’s Startup is open to:

- U.S. students enrolled as undergraduates in accredited U.S. colleges, universities, or trade schools

News influencers, newsfluencers or news creators – however you label them – are transforming how current events get shared and understood by the public. # 2026 Global Student Conference Travel Grant

The Internal Audit Foundation is proud to offer the Global Student Conference Travel Grant to support students and educators from around the world in attending the 2026 Global Student Conference (GSC).

This opportunity provides financial assistance for flights, accommodations, conference registration fees, and/or visa support as needed, ensuring that participants can engage fully with their peers and industry leaders at this premier event.

This grant is designed to ensure global representation, with priority given to applicants demonstrating both geographic diversity and financial need.

## 2026 Global Student Conference will be held April 19-21, 2026 in Orlando, Florida

Applications for the 2026 conference have closed. 2027 GSC Travel Grant applications will open Q3 2026.

## Who can apply for the Global Student Conference Travel Grant

### Students

Preference will be given to:

- Students who hold a valid passport.
- Students in disciplines related to internal audit.

### Educators

Preference will be given to:

- Faculty who hold a valid passport
- Faculty interested in expanding internal audit education.
- Faculty who currently teach or research internal audit.

# AnitaB.org Kamala Scholars

The AnitaB.org Kamala Scholars Program empowers the next generation of innovators by providing resources, mentorship, and access to Grace Hopper Celebration.

2026 Applications coming soon!

## About the Kamala Scholars Program

The Kamala Scholars Program is a year-long opportunity made possible through the generosity of an anonymous donor, in honor of a family member, and is dedicated to opening doors and creating pathways for 3rd- and 4th-year undergraduate students pursuing technical computing fields. AnitaB.org offers many opportunities to elevate the full diaspora of our community. This particular scholarship is focused exclusively on Black and Latine students, in alignment with the donor’s wishes. Each year, we welcome 100 students into the program.

### Scholars receive:

1

### Travel, Lodging & Transportation

Fully funded travel, lodging, and transportation to attend Grace Hopper Celebration

2

### AnitaB.org Membership

One year of Premium AnitaB.org Membership

3

### Career Coaching Sessions

12 one-on-one career coaching sessions for professional growth

As part of their commitment, selected scholars are required to attend GHC 26 in Anaheim, October 27-30, 2026, participate fully in their coaching sessions, and complete required program surveys.
